Byblos Resort

Hospitality · Byblos, Lebanon · 2026

How can every residence retain a meaningful relationship with the sea on a steep coastal site? The design begins with the terrain: stepped residential volumes avoid screening one another, while an internal spine organizes arrival, gardens and shared amenities without compromising privacy.

The site study translates the slope into terraced levels that open and protect view corridors while bringing daylight deep into the homes. Arrival begins from the upper road; independent residential access and vehicle circulation are absorbed along the site edge, leaving the central landscape calm and legible.

Shared pools, gardens, padel courts and pedestrian paths form a social layer, balanced by private terraces, gardens and plunge pools that give the residences protected outdoor space. Stone, timber and broad glazing connect the interiors to Mediterranean light and the coastal landscape.
